questions.q: Incidence of senile cataract per the book is:
questions.exp: Incidence: 50-70 years. (Book p76)

questions.q: Anticipation phenomenon in senile cataract per the book means:
opts: Later occurrence if family history present
Earlier occurrence if family history present
questions.exp: Anticipation phenomenon present (Earlier occurrence if family history present). (Book p76)

questions.q: Fill up: Increasing age → Oxidative damage to membranes & ___.
questions.exp: Increasing age → Oxidative damage to membranes & proteins. (Book p76)

questions.q: All are listed as risk factors for cataract formation per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Other risk factors: Sunlight (UV A + UV B) → Hydration, use of corticosteroids, increasing age oxidative damage, family history anticipation. (Book p76)

questions.q: Nuclear cataract is AKA ___ and loss of vision is:
questions.exp: Nuclear Cataract AKA central cataract; Loss of vision: Daytime > night. (Book p76)

questions.sec: Senile cataract — nuclear cataract daytime vs night
questions.q: A 65-year-old with central nuclear opacity complains vision worse in bright sunlight but can read menu in dim restaurant. Per the book's diagram, this is because:
opts: Daytime constricted pupil → light hits central opacity; Night dilated pupil → image via periphery
Night blindness due to rod dysfunction
questions.exp: Day time (Constricted pupil) Light rays Central opacity; Night time (Dilated pupil) Image is formed. (Book p76)

questions.q: Match second sight sequence per the book — 1) Sclerosis 2) ↑ RI of nucleus 3) Index myopia … A) Rigid/dense cataract of nucleus B) ↑ power of lens C) Near sighted, previously presbyopic/hypermetropic far sighted → second sight
questions.exp: Sclerosis → Rigid/dense cataract of nucleus → ↑ RI of nucleus → ↑ power of lens → Index myopia (Near sighted) → Previously presbyopic or hypermetropic patients (Far sighted) → Second sight phenomenon. (Book p76)

questions.q: Fill up: Second sight phenomenon is index ___ due to ↑ RI of sclerotic nucleus.
questions.exp: Index myopia (Near sighted) → Second sight phenomenon. (Book p76)

questions.q: A 62-year-old hypermetrope who needed +2.5 D reading glasses now reads without glasses, myopic shift noted. Per the book this second sight phenomenon is due to:
opts: Sclerosis ↑ RI of nucleus ↑ power → index myopia
questions.exp: Sclerosis Rigid/dense cataract nucleus ↑ RI → ↑ power lens → Index myopia (Near sighted) → Previously presbyopic/hypermetropic far sighted → Second sight phenomenon. (Book p76)

questions.q: Match nuclear cataract grading per the book — 1) Grade1 2) Grade2 3) Grade3 4) Grade4 … A) Yellow d/t urochrome pigment leads to xanthopsia B) Amber C) Brown cataracta brunescens D) Black cataracta nigra
questions.exp: Grade 1: Yellow (D/t urochrome pigment Leads to xanthopsia), Grade 2: Amber, Grade 3: Brown (Cataracta brunescens), Grade 4: Black (Cataracta nigra). (Book p77)

questions.q: Xanthopsia in Grade1 nuclear cataract is due to:
questions.exp: Grade 1: Yellow (D/t urochrome pigment Leads to xanthopsia). (Book p77)

questions.q: Which statement about oblique slit illumination is TRUE per the book's images?
opts: Normal lens shows anterior part, cornea, nucleus, posterior part of lens
questions.exp: Oblique slit illumination of normal lens labels Anterior part Cornea Nucleus Posterior part; Grade2/3 cataract labels Pupil Anterior capsule Nucleus Yellow/orange Cortex Anterior chamber. (Book p77)

questions.q: Cortical cataract per the book is:
opts: Central cataract with daytime > night loss
Peripheral cataract with night time (Nyctalopia) > daytime loss
questions.exp: Cortical Cataract: Peripheral cataract; Loss of vision: Night time (Nyctalopia/night blindness) > daytime. (Book p77)

questions.q: Match cortical cataract progression per the book — 1) Hydration 2) Cuneiform/immature senile 3) Mature/intumescent … A) Water clefts → Lamellar separation → Greyish white lens with iris shadow B) Pearly white, absence iris shadow d/t swollen lens, m/c complication phacomorphic glaucoma C) Clear spaces, wedge shaped opacities m/c inferonasally
questions.exp: Hydration water clefts → Lamellar separation → Cuneiform AKA immature senile cataract Greyish white colour presence iris shadow wedge shaped opacities clear spaces m/c inferonasally → Continuous hydration/swelling if not treated → Mature/intumescent Pearly white absence iris shadow d/t swollen lens m/c complication Phacomorphic glaucoma. (Book p77)

questions.q: Fill up: Cuneiform cataract shows clear spaces and ___ shaped opacities m/c inferonasally.
questions.exp: Clear spaces wedge shaped opacities Cuneiform cataract m/c inferonasally. (Book p77)

questions.q: A 70-year-old with greyish white lens and visible iris shadow progresses to pearly white lens with no iris shadow, swollen lens, IOP raised. Per the book, m/c complication at mature intumescent stage is:
questions.exp: Mature senile/intumescent: Pearly white absence iris shadow d/t swollen lens m/c complication Phacomorphic glaucoma. (Book p77)

questions.q: Three patients: A) Daytime worse than night, central yellow nucleus; B) Night worse than day, wedge opacities inferonasally; C) Glare at night, daytime near worse, max loss, nodal point. Per the book, A, B, C are:
opts: A Nuclear, B Cortical, C PSC
A Cortical, B Nuclear, C Anterior subcapsular
A PSC, B Nuclear, C Cortical
A Anterior subcapsular, B PSC, C Nuclear
questions.exp: Nuclear: Day > night, central; Cortical: Peripheral night > day wedge inferonasally; PSC: Glare day > night near > far max loss nodal point. (Book p77)

questions.q: Hypermature senile cataract is complete disintegration of cortical fibres d/t dysfunction of zonules and its m/c complication is:
questions.exp: Hypermature senile cataract Complete disintegration cortical fibres (D/t dysfunction zonules) m/c complication Subluxation of lens. (Book p78)

questions.q: Match hypermature variant — 1) Morgagnian 2) Sclerotic calcified … A) Liquefaction cortex → sinking nucleus → m/c complication phacolytic glaucoma B) Disintegrated cortex → leak through capsule → shrinkage with thickened anterior capsule C) Pearly white with iris shadow
questions.exp: Morgagnian: Liquefaction cortex Sinking nucleus m/c complication Phacolytic glaucoma; Sclerotic calcified: Disintegrated cortex Leak through capsule Shrinkage lens with thickened anterior capsule. (Book p78)

questions.q: Fill up: In morgagnian cataract, liquefaction of cortex leads to sinking of ___.
questions.exp: Morgagnian cataract: Liquefaction of cortex Sinking of nucleus m/c complication Phacolytic glaucoma. (Book p78)

questions.q: Photo series shows cortex and nucleus labels, then nucleus sinking inferiorly, then absorbed cortex with nucleus visible. Per the book this is variant of:
questions.exp: Variants of morgagnian cataract images Cortex Nucleus → Absorbed cortex Nucleus sinking. (Book p78)

questions.q: PSC per the book is AKA:
questions.exp: Posterior Subcapsular Cataract (PSC) AKA cupuliform cataract. (Book p78)

questions.q: All are clinical features of PSC per the book EXCEPT:
opts: Glare difficulty driving at night d/t bright light
Loss of vision daytime > night, near > far
Maximum loss of vision of all cataracts (opacity at nodal point)
questions.exp: PSC: Glare C/o difficulty driving at night d/t bright light; Loss Day > night, Near > far; Maximum loss of vision (Opacity at nodal point). Night > day is cortical. (Book p78)

questions.q: Match PSC pathology per the book — 1) Dysplasia of E cells 2) Posterior migration & enlargement 3) Bladder/Wedl cells … A) Collect to form plaque (Opacity) B) Equatorial cells dysplasia start C) Intermediate step
questions.exp: Pathology: Dysplasia of 'E' cells (Equatorial cells) → Posterior migration & enlargement → Bladder/Wedl cells: Collect to form plaque (Opacity). (Book p78)

questions.q: Fill up: In PSC, dysplasia of E cells leads to formation of ___ cells that form plaque.
questions.exp: Bladder/Wedl cells: Collect to form plaque (Opacity). (Book p78)

questions.sec: Senile cataract — etiology steroids and others
questions.q: Which statement about steroid-induced cataract/glaucoma is TRUE per the book?
opts: Systemic steroids cause glaucoma, topical cause cataract
Systemic steroids cause cataract, topical steroids cause glaucoma
Both systemic and topical cause only glaucoma
questions.exp: Etiology: Steroids: Systemic steroids: Cataract; Topical steroids: Glaucoma. (Book p79)

questions.q: All of the following are listed under other conditions causing cataract per p79 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Other conditions: Neurofibromatosis type 2, Myotonic dystrophy, Galactosemia, Blunt trauma, Complicated cataract primarily d/t uveitis/post uveitis, X-rays occupational ionizing radiation. (Book p79)

questions.q: Rarest form of cataract per the book is:
questions.exp: ANTERIOR SUBCAPSULAR CATARACT Rarest form of cataract. (Book p79)

questions.q: Fill up: Mnemonic AACG for anterior subcapsular cataract — Acute angle closure glaucoma: Glaukomflecken, Atopic dermatitis: Shield cataract, Amiodarone, Chlorpromazine, Gold ___.
questions.exp: Mnemonic AACG: Acute angle closure glaucoma: Glaukomflecken, Atopic dermatitis: Shield cataract, Amiodarone, Chlorpromazine, Gold deposits. (Book p79)

questions.q: Match anterior subcapsular cause with cataract name — 1) Acute angle closure glaucoma 2) Atopic dermatitis … A) Glaukomflecken B) Shield cataract C) Sunflower
questions.exp: Acute angle closure glaucoma: Glaukomflecken; Atopic dermatitis: Shield cataract. (Book p79)

questions.q: X-rays as etiology for cataract per the book refers to:
questions.exp: X-rays: Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation. (Book p79)

questions.q: Fill up: Complicated cataract as cause listed under senile cataract etiology is primarily d/t uveitis/___ uveitis.
questions.exp: Complicated cataract: Primarily d/t uveitis/post uveitis. (Book p79)
